## v1.0, or: I ported a Zelda game to Zig and all I got was this release page

A Link to the Past, running natively, now written in Zig, with actual downloadable binaries. Nobody asked for this. I did it anyway.

The heavy lifting came first, and it isn't mine: [snesrev/zelda3](https://github.com/snesrev/zelda3) spent years reverse engineering the whole game into C, from the title screen to the credits. I took that C, rewrote every line of it in Zig, and then kept going, because apparently I don't know when to stop.

No game data ships here. Bring your own US ROM. You know the drill, and so do the lawyers.

### What 46 commits of one person's free time gets you

**The whole thing is Zig now.** No MSVC project, no Makefile, just `zig build`. On the subject of Makefiles: the old CI was still building with one that had already been deleted. It's hard to beat a build that passes because it isn't building anything.

**Python is optional.** The asset importer is Zig now. It pulls graphics, music, dungeons, dialogue and every table the game needs straight out of your ROM in about a tenth of a second. The file it writes is byte-for-byte the one the old Python tool produced, and a test pins that digest, because an asset file that's "close enough" gives you bugs that look like game bugs, and those will eat a whole weekend.

**There's a launcher.** It edits the settings, builds the assets, checks they're the right ones, and starts the game. You can drive it with a keyboard, a gamepad or a mouse, and you can drop your ROM onto the window. It draws everything with SDL's built-in 8x8 font, so it looks like 1991, which is on theme.

A special mention goes to the bug where pressing A on a Nintendo controller *closed the launcher*. Nintendo puts A where everyone else puts B, and I lost an evening to that. The launcher now reads the label printed on the button, not where the button sits, and I have made my peace with it.

**SDL3.** Ported up from SDL2. Nothing exploded that I'm willing to admit to.

**Windows.** It builds and runs there now, with an icon, even. Getting the optimised Windows build through CI meant convincing Zig that mingw's security-hardened string functions weren't my problem. They weren't. It took a while anyway.

### Bugs I fixed that were technically older than the port

The port gets checked by running the original SNES machine code side by side with it and comparing the entire RAM, every single frame. It's a paranoid way to test, and it pays off:

- The bow could crash on the last frame of a shot. Very dramatic for a bow.
- Every save state was being written truncated. Every one. Great feature.
- The Debirando pit could fling Link across the room like he owed it money.
- Several tables got read past their ends: the bug net timer, the wall grab animations, the overworld offsets for special areas, the sword damage table when you had no sword, and the velocity-to-angle tables. None of them used to crash. They just quietly read the next table over, which is somehow worse.
- The mosaic effect could step out of bounds left of the visible line.
- The MSU warp cue now gets to finish before the music changes, instead of being cut off mid-song like an awards show speech.

### Release day, a short tragedy

My CI turned out to be failing on every commit for days, because the Zig setup action was asking for Zig downloads by a file name that stopped existing a couple of versions ago. I fixed that. Then GitHub warned me the action ran on a deprecated Node version, so I dropped it and wrote the download myself in about twenty lines of shell. Then Windows broke on the actual release build. It's fixed. It all works. I am fine.

### Getting it running

1. Download the archive for your system and unpack it anywhere.
2. Start `zelda3-launcher`.
3. Drag your ROM onto the window when it asks, or put it next to the launcher as `zelda3.sfc`.
4. Press Launch. The first run builds `zelda3_assets.dat`, and after that the ROM can go back in the drawer.

Per platform:

- **Windows (x86_64):** `SDL3.dll` is included. SmartScreen will act like you've downloaded a virus, because nobody has paid Microsoft to vouch for me. Click "More info", then "Run anyway".
- **macOS (Apple Silicon):** SDL3 is included. The binaries aren't notarised, because that costs $99 a year and this is a hobby. macOS will block them the first time. Run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine alttp-zig` on the unpacked folder, or allow them under System Settings → Privacy & Security.
- **Linux (x86_64):** you need SDL3 from your package manager: `libsdl3-0` on Ubuntu 25.10 or newer, `SDL3` on Fedora, `sdl3` on Arch. You're on Linux. You'll be fine.

Settings live in `zelda3.ini` next to the binaries, and the launcher edits them for you.

If something breaks, open an issue. If something breaks in an interesting way, open an issue and brag about it.
